ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p160/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p160/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p160/r3.claim: Moses's staff becoming a snake was the great sign; apart from the white hand, the other miracles were concealed in and manifested through it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p160/r3.anchor: except for the miracle of the white hand all other miracles were concealed in it and manifested themselves through it

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r16.claim: The great sign is Moses' staff becoming a serpent, a proof of resurrection and of the creative command “Be.”
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r16.anchor: Âyet-i kübra o büyük mucize, asânın dirilip yılan olması mucizesidir ki ölülerin dirilmesine ve كُنْ emrinin tecellîsine bir burhandır.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r17.claim: When Pharaoh did not heed verbal evidence, Moses demonstrated the truth through a physical sign.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r17.anchor: Kavlî delîli dinlemeyince fiilî olarak bunu gösterdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r3.claim: The greatest miracle Moses showed Pharaoh was his staff turning into a snake.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r3.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ’nın Firavun’a gösterdiği en büyük mûcizeden maksat yılana dönüşen asasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r4.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r4.claim: Some exegetes say Moses’s greatest miracle was his shining hand.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r4.anchor: Müfessirler bu mûcizenin, Mûsâ’nın ışık saçan eli

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r5.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r5.claim: Some exegetes say Moses’s greatest miracle was the parting of the sea.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r6.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r6.claim: Some exegetes say it was all nine miracles given to Moses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r6.anchor: Mûsâ’ya verilen dokuz mûcizenin tamamı olabileceğini de söylemişlerdir

QASHANI:79:18-26/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:18-26/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:18-26/r2.claim: The greatest sign was the true identity, given through intellectual unity and divine guidance; Pharaoh failed to see it because his veil and delusion were too strong to admit a higher station.
QASHANI:79:18-26/r2.anchor: فأراه الآية الكبرى } أي: الهوية الحقيقية بالتوحيد العلمي والهداية الحقانية فلم يرها لقوة حجابه ورسوخ توهمه

BINTSHATI:v1p145/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r1.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r1.claim: Some exegetes considered the hand the greater sign because the next phrase calls it one of the greatest signs.
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r1.anchor: وقيل فيما قيل: إن اليد أعظم في الإعجاز من العصا لأنه عقب على ذكر اليد بقوله: لنريك من آياتنا اكبرى.

BINTSHATI:v1p145/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r2.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r2.claim: Others considered the staff greater because it changed color, became alive, and gained power while inanimate.
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r2.anchor: وقيل: بل العصا أعظم، لأنه ليس في اليد إلا تغيير اللون، وأما العصا ففيها تغيير اللون، وخلق الحياة والقدرة في الجماد،

BINTSHATI:v1p145/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies the staff becoming a serpent as the principal sign, with the hand as its dependent companion.
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r3.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: "الآية الكبرى قلب العصا حية، لأنها كانت المقدمة والأصل، والأخرى - يعني اليد - كالتبع لها

BINTSHATI:v1p145/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows both signs to count as one, since the hand is subordinate to the staff.
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r4.anchor: الزمخشري: "الآية الكبرى قلب العصا حية، لأنها كانت المقدمة والأصل، والأخرى - يعني اليد - كالتبع لها لأن موسى كان يتقيها بيده، أو أرادهما جميعاً،

BINTSHATI:v1p145/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan likewise treats the staff and hand together as one sign because the hand follows the staff.
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حيان: "الآية الكبرى هي العصا واليد معاً، جعلهما آية واحدة، لأن اليد كأنها من جملة العصا لكونها تابعة لها

BINTSHATI:v1p145/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r6.claim: The author leaves the sign unidentified, following the Qur’an’s own choice to call it the great sign and emphasizing its proof of Moses and God’s power.
BINTSHATI:v1p145/r6.anchor: والأولى ألا نحدد الآية هنا، ما دام القرآن نفسه لم ير تعيينها في هذا الموضع، مكتفياً بوصفها بالكبرى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r1.claim: After Pharaoh demanded proof and doubted Moses' exceptional status despite having raised him, Moses showed a sign proving his message.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r1.anchor: فطلب الدليل على صحة الرسالة واستبعد أن يختص عنه بهذه المنزلة العلية وقد رباه وليدا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r2.claim: One identification of the great sign is the staff becoming a serpent.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r2.anchor: وهي قلب العصا حية أو جميع معجزاته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r3.claim: Another identification of the great sign is all of Moses' miracles.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r3.anchor: قلب العصا حية أو جميع معجزاته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r22.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r22.claim: Mujahid and others identify the great sign as Moses’s staff and hand, displayed in challenge and defeating the false party.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r22.anchor: والآية الكبرى: العصا واليد، قاله مجاهد وغيره، وهما نصب موسى للتحدي

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r7.claim: The verse shows that proof becomes binding only when a miracle appears.
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r7.anchor: ويدل قوله: (فأراه الآية) أن الحجة إنما تلزم بظهور المعجز

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r8.claim: The great sign shown to Pharaoh was the hand and the staff.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r8.anchor: وهي اليد والعصا أخرج يده بيضاء

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r9.claim: The hand shone like the sun and dazzled the eye; it was greater and more wondrous than the staff, without leprosy.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r9.anchor: لها شعاع كشعاع الشمس يغشى البصر، فكانت اليد أعظم وأعجب من العصا من غير سوء يعني من غير برص،

NAHHAS:v5p143/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p143/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p143/r11.claim: The term in this verse must have the definite article; it cannot appear without the article or as an indefinite noun.
NAHHAS:v5p143/r11.anchor: مما لا يجوز حذف الألف واللام منه ولا يؤتى به نكرة

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r6.claim: Although another account mentions nine clear signs, it does not identify which one was the greatest sign.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r6.anchor: One account mentions nine clear signs (17:101), but does not state which is the greatest sign

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r7.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r7.claim: The greatest sign may have been Moses' staff turning into a serpent.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r7.anchor: Some say it is the staff that became a serpent (7:107; 20:66–17; 26:32, 44–45)

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r8.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r8.claim: The greatest sign may have been Moses' hand turning white.

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r9.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r9.claim: The greatest sign may have been the parting of the sea.

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r10.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r10.claim: Alternatively, the greatest sign may refer to all the miracles Moses performed.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r10.anchor: or all of the miracles that Moses performed.

TABRISI:79:15-24/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:15-24/r15.claim: The greatest sign shown to Pharaoh is the staff.

TABRISI:79:15-24/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r16.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:79:15-24/r16.claim: Hasan identifies the greatest sign as Moses' shining hand.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r1.claim: The great sign shown to Pharaoh was Moses’ shining white hand.

ASAD-NOTES:79:20#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:20#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:20#n9/r1.claim: The great sign is God's guidance, offered through measureless grace even to the most recalcitrant sinner.
ASAD-NOTES:79:20#n9/r1.anchor: "showed him the great wonder", i.e., of the guidance which God, in His measureless grace, offers even to the most recalcitrant sinner.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#2/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies Moses' great sign as his staff and hand.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#2/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ الآية الكبرى ﴾ قال عصاه ويده

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r1.claim: The clause compresses omitted events—Moses went and did what followed—relying on the fuller account elsewhere; al-Zamakhsharī supplies only ‘he went,’ implied by the command ‘go.’
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r1.anchor: فصيحة تفصح عن جمل قد طويت تعويلا على تفصيلها في موضع آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī supplies ‘he went’ before ‘he showed him,’ comparing the ellipsis to the staff striking the rock followed by water gushing out.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r2.anchor: واقتصر الزمخشري في الحواشي على تقدير جملة فقال إن هذا معطوف على محذوف والتقدير فذهب فأراه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r3.claim: The verb of showing may mean making Pharaoh see or acquainting him; once Pharaoh saw the sign he recognized it, and his claim that it was magic only feigned bravado.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r3.anchor: والإراءة إما بمعنى التبصير أو بمعنى التعريف فإن اللعين حين أبصرها عرفها وادعاء سحريتها إنما كان إظهارا للتجلد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r4.claim: Attributing the signs to Moses is according to outward appearance, while their true source is God, who says ‘We showed him Our signs.’
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r4.anchor: ونسبتها إليه عليه الصلاة والسلام بالنظر إلى الظاهر كما أن نسبتها إلى نون العظمة في قوله تعالى ولقد أريناه آياتنا بالنظر إلى الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the great sign as Moses’ staff turning into a serpent, the primary miracle to which the other sign was subsidiary.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r5.anchor: والمراد بالآية الكبرى على ما روي عن ابن عباس قلب العصاحية فإنها كانت المقدمة والأصل والأخرى كالتبع لها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r6.claim: Mujāhid identifies the great sign as both the staff and the shining hand, whose combined evidentiary force makes them one sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r6.anchor: وعلى ما روي عن مجاهد وذلك واليد البيضاء فإنهما باعتبار الدلالة كالآية الواحدة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r7.claim: The two signs are plural in the command to Moses and his brother because each contains several wondrous, clear signs for rational people.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r7.anchor: وقد عبر عنهما بصيغة الجمع في قوله تعالى اذهب أنت وأخوك بآياتي باعتبار ما في تضاعيفهما منبدائع الأمور التي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r8.claim: Other proposals take the great sign as all of Moses’ miracles, treating them as one collective sign or referring to the group by its first instance; its greatness may be relative to earlier prophets’ miracles or absolute, though al-Ālūsī finds the latter less plausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r8.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بها مجموع معجزاته عليه السلام والوحدة باعتبار ما ذكر والفاء لتعقيب أولها أو مجموعها باعتبار أولها وكونها كبرى باعتبار معجزات من قبله من الرسل عليهم السلام أو هو للزيادة المطلقة ولا يخفى بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r9.claim: The magicians were assembled only after the staff and hand were shown; the remaining nine signs came after Moses defeated the magicians, over roughly twenty years, which weighs against taking the verse for all the miracles.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r9.anchor: ويزيده بعدا ترتيب حشر السحرة بعد فإنه لم يكن إلا على إراءة تينك الآيتين وإدباره عن العمل بمقتضاهما

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r10.speaker: غلاة الشيعة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects extremist Shīʿī claims that the great sign was ʿAlī appearing to Moses in a transformed spiritual state as irrational and unsupported by transmitted tradition.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#5/r10.anchor: وزعم غلاة الشيعة أن الآية الكبرى علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أراه إياه متطورة روحه الكريمة بأعظم طور وهو هذيان وراء العقل وطور النقل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#5/r1.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#5/r1.claim: The majority of commentators identify the great sign as both the hand and the staff.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#5/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنها اليد والعصا قاله جمهور المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#5/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#5/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj identifies the great sign as the hand alone.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r10.claim: Moses showed a powerful proof and clear evidence that his message came from God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r10.anchor: {فأراه الآية الكبرى} يعني: فأظهر له موسى مع هذه الدعوة الحق حجة قوية، ودليلا واضحا على صدق ما جاءه به من عند الله،

MUJAHID:v2p727#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p727#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v2p727#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan identifies Moses' great sign as his hand and staff.
MUJAHID:v2p727#2/r1.anchor: سألت الحسن عن قوله ﴿ فأراه الآية الكبرى ﴾ قال يعني يده وعصاه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#11/r1.claim: Moses showed Pharaoh the staff, or the staff and the shining hand, since together they count as one sign.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#11/r1.anchor: أي فذهب فأرى موسى فرعون العصا أو العصا واليد البيضاء لأنهما فى حكم آية واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r1.claim: The fāʾ coordinates the clause with an understood “he went”: “then he went and showed him,” as in the omitted “he struck” before the rock split.
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r1.anchor: معطوف على محذوف معلوم ، يعني فذهب فأراه

RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r2.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r2.claim: Maqātil and al-Kalbī identify the great sign as Moses’ hand, citing the hand turning white and the sign shown to Pharaoh.

RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r3.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ identifies the sign as the staff: the hand only changed color, while the staff became alive, grew, swallowed objects, and then lost its life and form.
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r3.anchor: هي العصا ، لأنه ليس في اليد إلا انقلاب لونه

RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r4.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r4.claim: Mujāhid takes the great sign to be the hand and staff together, since Moses first showed Pharaoh the staff and then the hand.
RAZI-FULL:v31p38/r4.anchor: وهو أن المراد من الآية الكبرى مجموع اليد والعصا

TAB-FULL:v24p82/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r1.claim: Moses showed Pharaoh the great proof of his prophethood: his hand appearing white and his staff turning into a manifest serpent.
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r1.anchor: سمعت الحسن، يقول في هذه الآية: {فأراه الآية الكبرى}

TAB-FULL:v24p82/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the great sign as Moses' hand and staff.
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r2.anchor: سمعت الحسن، يقول في هذه الآية: {فأراه الآية الكبرى}

TAB-FULL:v24p82/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies the sign as Moses' staff and hand.

TAB-FULL:v24p82/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r4.claim: Qatāda says Pharaoh saw Moses' hand and staff, two signs.

TAB-FULL:v24p82/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the signs as the staff and serpent.
TAB-FULL:v24p82/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فأراه الآية الكبرى}

TABATABAI:79:19-22/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r5.claim: The fāʾ is explanatory and the sentence elides “he came to him and called him” before saying that he showed him the sign.
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r5.anchor: الفاء فصيحة وفي الكلام حذف وتقدير والأصل فأتاه ودعاه فأراه

TABATABAI:79:19-22/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r6.claim: The great sign is apparently the staff, based on the detailed account; identifying it with all the miracles shown to Pharaoh and his chiefs is remote.
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r6.anchor: على ما يظهر من تفصيل القصة آية العصا، وقيل المراد بها مجموع معجزاته

BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh recognized the sign on seeing it; his later claim that it was magic only displayed stubbornness.
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r1.anchor: حين أبصرها عرفها وادعاء سحريتها إنما كان إراءة منه وإظهارا للتجلد

BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r2.claim: Attributing the signs to Moses reflects outward appearance, whereas attributing them to God in 20:56 reflects the ultimate reality.
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r2.anchor: ونسبتها إليه بالنظر إلى الظاهر كما أن نسبتها إلى نون العظمة

BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r3.claim: The great sign was the staff’s transformation into a serpent; the other remaining miracles were lesser signs, and the sequence suggests this sign was shown first.
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالآية الكبرى قلب العصاحية والصغرى غيره من معجزاته الباقية

QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r6.claim: The great sign was Moses' hand emerging white and shining like the sun; Pharaoh consulted Haman, who warned that he would lose his lordship and kingship if he became subject.
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r6.anchor: هي إخراج يده بيضاء لها شعاع كشعاع الشمس . فقال فرعون : حتى أشاور هامان ، فشاوره

BURHAN:v2p515/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p515/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p515/r8.claim: Though فعلى is originally adjectival, as القصوى and الكبرى show, it often functions like a noun, as الأبطح, الأجرع, and الأدهم do.
BURHAN:v2p515/r8.anchor: والفعلى في هذا الباب وإن كانت في الاصل صفة بدليل قوله تعالى ﴿ وهم بالعدوة القصوى ﴾

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r7.claim: The great sign may mean the staff and hand together, with the hand subordinate to the staff.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r7.anchor: وهي العصا واليد، جعلهما واحدة، لأن اليد كأنها من جملة العصا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r8.claim: Alternatively it is the staff alone as principal sign, the hand being secondary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r8.anchor: أو العصا وحدها لأنها كانت المقدمة والأصل، واليد تبع لها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r11.claim: The great sign was the staff and the shining white hand.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r7.claim: The greatest sign may be the staff turning into a serpent, as the first and central miracle, or all his miracles considered one sign because of their shared proof.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r7.anchor: فذهب وبلغ فأراه المعجزة الكبرى وهي قلب العصا حية

BINTSHATI:v1p144/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r6.claim: An āya is a sign, often used religiously for proof of God's existence, greatness, unity, power, or the miracles supporting chosen messengers; here it proves Moses was sent by God.
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r6.anchor: الآية: العلامة، ويكثر استعمالها - دينياً - في الدلالة على وجود الله

BINTSHATI:v1p144/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r7.claim: Calling the sign “great” magnifies the force of its proof and its support for Moses' mission; to identify it, Bint al-Shati turns to Moses' call in Ṭā Hā.
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r7.anchor: ووصفت الآية بالكبرى تعظيماً وتقريراً لقوة دلالتها وبلوغها في تأييد رسالة موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r2.claim: The fa before showing the great sign is explanatory of omitted events after the command: Moses went, called Pharaoh, was rejected, and then showed the sign.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r2.anchor: الفاء في قوله : { فأراه الآية الكبرى } فصيحة وتفريع على محذوف يقتضيه قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r3.claim: The great sign is the staff becoming a manifest serpent, as related in the account where Pharaoh challenges Moses to bring a clear proof.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r3.anchor: فتلك هي الآية الكبرى المرادة هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r4.claim: An aya is a sign or marker, then by extension evidence establishing truth, and in this context a messenger's miracle proving his truthfulness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r4.anchor: والآية : حقيقتها العلامة والأمارة ، وتطلق على الحجة المثبتة لأنها علامة على ثبوت الحق

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r12.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r12.claim: The great sign is Moses’ staff and hand.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r12.anchor: أنها عصاه ويده ، قاله الحسن وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r13.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r13.claim: The great sign refers to Paradise and Hell.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r14.claim: A third possibility is God’s speech to Moses from the tree.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r14.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : أنه كلامه من الشجرة

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r19.claim: The great sign means the supreme miracle.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r20.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r20.claim: Some identify the sign as the staff, others the bright hand shining like the sun.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r20.anchor: وقيل: العصا. وقيل: اليد البيضاء تبرق كالشمس

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r21.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits Ibn Abbas’s view that it was the staff; al-Hasan says hand and staff.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r21.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس: الآية الكبرى قال العصا. الحسن: يده وعصاه

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r22.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r22.claim: Other views identify the sign as the splitting of the sea or all of Moses’ signs and miracles.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r22.anchor: وقيل: فلق البحر. وقيل: الآية: إشارة إلى جميع آياته ومعجزاته
